definition: Chroma is an open-source embedding database that stores documents with their vectors and metadata and finds the closest matches.
details: Created by Jeff Huber and Anton Troynikov in 2022; developed by Chroma (Chroma Inc.). It runs in-process, as a server or as Chroma Cloud.

explainer.lead: How to install ChromaDB, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.createdBy: Jeff Huber and Anton Troynikov; Chroma Inc.

quickstart.python:
import chromadb

client = chromadb.Client()
notes = client.create_collection("notes")
notes.add(ids=["1", "2"], documents=["Cats purr when happy.", "GPUs speed up training."])
print(notes.query(query_texts=["why do kittens purr"], n_results=1)["documents"])

explainer.inAi: The simplest way to add retrieval to a prototype: it embeds documents for you with a default model.

tiers.eli5: It's like a filing cabinet that also remembers what each document is about, so you can ask 'what's most similar to this?' and get the nearest files back.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as the retrieval store in retrieval-augmented generation, running it in-process, as a server or via Chroma Cloud. A pitfall is assuming stored metadata and vectors stay in sync as documents change.
tiers.paperLevel: An embedding database holding documents with vectors and metadata, answering nearest-match queries; created by Jeff Huber and Anton Troynikov in 2022 and developed by Chroma Inc. Its scope is similarity search over stored embeddings.

explainer.example: A RAG system embeds support articles into Chroma and, at query time, retrieves the closest documents to feed the model.
